candidate.blueprint_topic: Pharmacological and Parenteral Therapies — medication safety, administration and monitoring
candidate.educational_objective: During parenteral nutrition, monitor glucose as part of the PN safety plan and respond to persistent hyperglycemia through clinical reassessment and coordinated management.

options.A: Ignore the glucose trend because parenteral nutrition does not require glucose monitoring once the infusion is established.
options.B: Remove the central venous catheter because hyperglycemia by itself confirms a catheter-related bloodstream infection.
options.C: Increase the dextrose delivery to correct the elevated glucose before notifying the nutrition or prescribing team.
options.D: Continue the prescribed PN monitoring process, report the glucose trend, and collaborate on measures to restore glucose control while separately assessing for other clinical problems.

candidate.rationale: ASPEN’s Parenteral Nutrition Care Pathway directs clinicians to initiate a monitoring protocol, reevaluate PN therapy, and maintain glucose control as part of PN quality and safety. An elevated glucose trend therefore requires assessment and management rather than being ignored, treated by increasing dextrose, or used alone to diagnose a catheter infection.
candidate.source_claim_supported: ASPEN PN care requires monitoring/re-evaluation and maintenance of glucose control; CLABSI prevention is a separate PN quality domain.
candidate.source_locator: Step 9 “Monitor and Reevaluate Patient” (initiate monitoring protocol; evaluate efficacy/goals) and Step 11 “Parenteral Nutrition Quality Improvement Program” (maintain glucose control; infection control for CLABSI listed separately)
candidate.source_organization: American Society for Parenteral and Enteral Nutrition (ASPEN)
candidate.source_version_date: PN Care Pathway listed by ASPEN as 04/2025; live pathway rechecked 2026-08-16
candidate.stem: A hospitalized adult receiving parenteral nutrition has repeated blood-glucose values above the prescribed goal. Which nursing response best reflects current PN safety guidance?
